doc.title: Fred Staton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 12, 2008

title: Dancing, Lindy hop and swing bands on film
summary: Dancers did Lindy hop and swing at his gigs; discussion of whether swing band shorts were seen in movie houses.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Sure. When you were playing gigs with the band at that time, it was for dancing, right?
Yeah.
People danced. They didn’t really sit and listen.
They danced, yes.
Yeah. What kind of dances were they doing?
Lindy hop.
Things like we see pictures of it at the Savoy Ballroom and that kind of stuff.
That type. Not the throwing up and all that kind of stuff from the Savoy, but that type. Swing dancing.
I’ve seen some neat, some of the video from back then, like with the Count Basie Orchestra.
At the Savoy?

Yeah. And they’d have these funny things with, they were almost like just little story lines, of Jimmy Rushing being on the dance floor and he’s the last one standing or something. Were those things used in the movie houses? It seemed like they were just short pieces of some of the swing bands playing, and I wondered, where would you see them back in the thirties and forties.
That’s a good question. We wouldn’t see them. They weren’t there. No.
So if you went to the movies—
You wouldn’t see them.
No?
No.
I don’t know what they used them for. I guess some of them were on what they called the kinescopes or something, like they had a juke box that you actually could see a little video.
Oh yeah. Yeah, yeah. That, yeah.
Okay.
But for the movies, no.
